Re-encoding some 1440p h264 video in h265, to use a target file size it makes you do a 2-pass encode. Why? What's being done in the second pass and why can't it be done in the first?
How does 2-pass video encoding work and why can't you do what it does in 1 pass?

A good analogy is single pass would be akin to ripping a CD to raw format, 2-pass would be ripping it to mp3 with variable bitrate.

2-pass would compress the data for scenes that are all black (for example in a fade to black transition). Those few frames that are all black do not need to be raw data and can afford to be compressed.

I'll add to sakuramboo, the first pass is an analysis pass, basically it checks to see how difficult each part of the video is to encode, then the second pass allocates the storage according to the first pass.

you should just use crf, it will give the same quality but (you are right) it can't set a target size. crf basically tells it "make it this quality" and then when a part takes more space, it simply takes more space.

you could think of the first pass as figuring out what is going to take up space, and the second pass as the actual encoding.
